notes: Returns the newly created array, but it is already attached to `object` and is freed by cJSON_Delete on the root. Freeing the return separately is a double free. Same cJSON* return type as cJSON_CreateArray, opposite ownership - the central hazard of the paper.

signature: c_int cJSON_AddItemToObject(c_void_p object, c_char_p string, c_void_p item)
notes: Returns bool, so owner=na. But ownership of `item` TRANSFERS into `object`: after this call the caller must not cJSON_Delete(item). The enum has no value for an ownership-transferring PARAMETER; label_owner only covers the return.

signature: c_void_p cJSON_AddNumberToObject(c_void_p object, c_char_p name, c_double number)
notes: Same pattern as cJSON_AddArrayToObject: new node owned by the parent tree.
Caller must cJSON_Delete. `numbers` is a const double* input sized by `count`, so the readable extent is stated and it is bindable. The sheet signature renders it c_void_p*, losing the element type.
Caller must cJSON_Delete the returned tree.

signature: c_void_p cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(c_char_p value, c_ulong buffer_length, c_void_p return_parse_end, c_int require_null_terminated)
notes: Return must be cJSON_Delete'd. `return_parse_end` is a const char** set to a pointer INTO the caller's input buffer: it must never be freed and dangles as soon as the input is released.

signature: c_void_p cJSON_ParseWithOpts(c_char_p value, c_void_p return_parse_end, c_int require_null_terminated)
notes: As ParseWithLengthOpts; return_parse_end aliases the caller's input buffer.

signature: c_int cJSON_PrintPreallocated(c_void_p item, c_void_p buffer, c_int length, c_int format)
notes: `length` states the buffer size and print_buffer runs with noalloc, so an oversize write fails rather than overflowing - safe to bind. Docs warn the required size is not exactly predictable (allocate ~5 bytes slack), so a binding must surface the false return rather than assume success.

signature: c_int cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject(c_void_p object, c_char_p string, c_void_p newitem)
notes: Hesitated. It silently cJSON_Delete's the item it replaces and takes ownership of `newitem`. Labelled `uses` because the destroyed handle is not a parameter, but any caller still holding a pointer to the old item now has a dangling pointer. `destroys` is defensible.
Raw allocator: caller must cJSON_free, which is not necessarily free() if cJSON was built with custom hooks. Returns untyped memory rather than a cJSON handle, hence lifecycle=na.
